claims.explanation: GW-583340 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitor, so sensitivity is likely driven by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling. The most sensitive lines include EGFR-mutant lung cancers (HCC4006, NCIH1650) and other lines with potential ERBB2 activation, while resistant lines often lack EGFR/ERBB2 alterations or have mutations in downstream effectors like KRAS, BRAF, or NRAS that bypass receptor inhibition. Thus, EGFR/ERBB2 mutation or high expression, and lack of downstream MAPK pathway mutations, predict selective killing.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR inhibitors; observed in sensitive lung lines HCC4006 and NCIH1650.
ERBB2 is a direct target; mutations or amplification can confer sensitivity to dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitors.
High EGFR expression may increase dependence on EGFR signaling and sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors.
High ERBB2 expression can sensitize cells to ERBB2-targeted therapies.
KRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling, bypassing EGFR/ERBB2 inhibition; observed in resistant lines like CL11 and MKN1.
BRAF mutations can drive resistance to upstream receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors; observed in resistant melanoma lines.
NRAS mutations activate MAPK pathway independently of EGFR/ERBB2; observed in resistant lines KU1919 and IPC298.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling, potentially bypassing EGFR/ERBB2 dependence; observed in resistant lines like UACC62 and FTC133.
PIK3CA mutations can activate PI3K pathway and reduce dependence on EGFR/ERBB2; observed in resistant lines HGC27 and MKN1.
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling, bypassing receptor inhibition; observed in resistant lines like LOXIMVI and BICR6.
MAP2K1 mutations activate downstream MAPK, conferring resistance to EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitors; observed in resistant line NCIH1437.
MET alterations can bypass EGFR/ERBB2 inhibition; observed in resistant line HGC27.
